subject: physics
title: Thermal expansion
key_idea: Solids, liquids and gases expand when they are heated and contract when they are cooled. Gases expand the most and solids the least. Particles move faster and spread further apart; they do not get bigger.

sections.heading: Expansion of solids, liquids and gases

blocks.text: Most materials get bigger when they are heated. This section covers how the three states compare.

items.meaning: The increase in size of a material when its temperature rises.

items: Solids, liquids and gases all **expand** when heated and **contract** when cooled.
A gas expands at constant pressure when it is heated.
**Gases** expand the most, **liquids** expand less and **solids** expand the least.
The expansion of a solid is small, but it can be very large for a long object.
All three states expand when heated and contract when cooled.
Gas expands most and solid expands least.

blocks.text: Expansion is useful in some devices and a problem in some structures.

rows: The liquid expands as it warms, so it rises up the narrow tube.
Two metals expand by different amounts, so the strip bends. It can switch a thermostat on and off.
Running hot water over the lid makes it expand and come loose.
Railway lines can buckle in hot weather
Small gaps are left between the rails.
Bridges can crack as they expand
Expansion joints or rollers allow the bridge to move.
Power cables sag in hot weather and are tight in cold weather
Cables are hung with some slack.

items: Thermometers and thermostats use expansion.
Gaps, joints and slack cables allow for expansion.

blocks.text: (Supplement) The particle model explains why materials expand and why gases expand the most.

items: Heating gives the particles more energy in their kinetic store.
In a solid the particles vibrate more. In a liquid or gas they move faster.
The average separation of the particles increases, so the material takes up more space.
The particles themselves do not get bigger, and their number does not change.

items: In a solid, strong forces hold the particles close, so they can only move apart a little.
In a liquid the forces are weaker, so the particles can move further apart.
In a gas the forces are almost zero, so the particles spread out the most.
Heating makes the particles move or vibrate more, so they spread further apart.
Weaker forces between particles mean greater expansion.

checks.q: State which state of matter has the greatest thermal expansion and which has the least.
checks.a: Gas has the greatest expansion and solid has the least.

checks.q: Give one problem caused by thermal expansion and how it is overcome.
checks.a: Rails buckle in hot weather, so gaps are left between rails. (Bridges have expansion joints.)

checks.q: (Supplement) Explain, in terms of particles, why a gas expands more than a solid when heated.
checks.a: The forces between gas particles are almost zero, so they can move much further apart. In a solid, strong forces hold the particles close together.

worked_example.question: An aluminium dish is initially at room temperature. Boiling water is poured into the dish. Explain, in terms of its particles, why the aluminium expands.
answer_points: The particles gain energy in their kinetic store as the temperature of the aluminium increases.
The average separation of the aluminium particles increases (the particles move further apart).
worked_example.tip: One mark for the particles gaining energy and one for the separation increasing.
